acceptanceCriteria: Controlled concurrent finish calls for one Work Item do not produce raw filesystem race artifacts and leave authoritative JSON records valid.
Atomic writes use unique same-process temporary identities, verified by repeated concurrent fault-injection runs.
Finish, archive, close, retry, and projection-recovery behavior records commit authority and does not display an incomplete operation as completed.
Duplicate operation attempts are idempotent or fail with an explicit conflict without duplicating history or granting authorization.
Any remaining rollback or crash-consistency limitation is demonstrated, documented, and represented as an unknown or blocked state rather than hidden.
goal: Establish evidence-backed multi-file consistency, idempotency, concurrency, and recovery behavior for lifecycle operations, including a real fix for the same-process atomic-write collision and explicit handling of any remaining rollback-clobber risk.
intent: Re-deliver the P2-C lifecycle concurrency and recovery investigation from the latest default branch, with controlled fault injection covering finish, archive, close, retry, and projection recovery; repair only proven unsafe behavior and preserve existing contracts.
outOfScope: Changing public JSON schemas, exit codes, or unrelated lifecycle commands without a demonstrated P2-C failure
Replacing the repository storage system, introducing a database, microservice, or broad event-sourcing framework
Modifying other agents worktrees, branches, contracts, evidence, or archived Work Items
